Certified type:
- Category: density sensor (a sensor as a part of a densitometer) - hmm, the schema category examples: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter", ... For R117-1 (Dynamic measuring systems for liquids other than water). The certified type is a "density sensor". I'll use "Density sensor" or perhaps "Measuring system"? Let me use "Density sensor (part of a densitometer)" — actually the description says "A density sensor (a sensor as a part of a densitometer)". Category: "Density sensor". Type designations: CDM100M, CDM100P.

Recommendation:
- R 117-1 (2007) — canonical id "R117-1", edition 2007? The schema says edition (int). Hmm, R117-1 (2007) — edition could be 2007. Accuracy class: 0.3. Actually the "0,3" is the accuracy class for this density sensor. Actually in R117, class 0.3. The MPE is 0.8 kg/m³.

Wait — R117-1 is a 2007 edition. The certificate number is R117/2007-NL1-15.01. So recommendation id "R117-1", edition 2007, accuracy_classes ["0.3"].

Scheme: this is a single certificate (scheme A?). OIML certificates — the schema says scheme (A|B). This is a standard OIML Certificate of Conformity — scheme A. Actually for OIML-CS, there are two schemes: A (basic) and B (MAA). This is an NMi issued cert under the older OIML certificate system. Default to "A".

Test reports:
- No. NMi-12200566-01 dated 13 April 2015, 114 pages, role: type_evaluation_report

Models: two types CDM100M and CDM100P, differing in material. These are two type variants. Should I create a model_family? The cert covers 2 model variants (CDM100M, CDM100P). The characteristics listed apply to both types (no per-model variation given). The schema says model_family: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. There are two types listed: CDM100M; CDM100P. So include model_family with models [{"model_id": "CDM100M", "attributes": {"material": "Stainless Steel"}}, {"model_id": "CDM100P", "attributes": {"material": "Nickel alloy C22 (N06022)"}}].

Hmm, but are CDM100M and CDM100P separate models or just type designations? They differ in material. I'll treat them as models with material attribute.

Components: External Supply 1 and External Supply 2 are sub-assemblies (alternative power supply options). They could be recorded as components with alternatives "OR". Let me record:
- components[]: 
  - {role: "external_supply", type_designations: ["QUINT PS/1AC/24 VDC/3.5"], alternatives: null, characteristics: {...}}
  - {role: "external_supply", type_designations: ["QUINT PS/24 VDC/24 VDC/5"], ...}

Since these are two separate options, they could be alternatives: "OR" — the cert says power supply "either from flow computer or external power supply", and there are two external supplies listed. Actually the two external supplies are alternatives. I could group them: components entry with alternatives "OR"? The schema for components has role, type_designations[], alternatives. Hmm, type_designations is a list. I could do one component with role "external_power_supply" and type_designations ["QUINT PS/1AC/24 VDC/3.5", "QUINT PS/24 VDC/24 VDC/5"], alternatives "OR". But the characteristics differ per supply. Better: two separate components entries, each with its own characteristics. Alternatives could be "OR" for both since they're alternative options. I'll mark both as alternatives "OR" — or maybe leave null. I think listing two entries with alternatives "OR" is reasonable. Actually, to be safe, I'll do two components entries, both role "external_power_supply", each with alternatives "OR" indicating they are alternatives to each other. Hmm, that's a bit awkward. Let me think: the schema example: "Transmitter UMC4 OR UMC4-RM" → alternatives: "OR". So a single component entry with two type_designations and alternatives "OR". But characteristics differ... The characteristics field is a dict. I could include power supply characteristics per component. I'll go with two separate entries each alternatives: "OR", since they're alternatives offered.

Actually, simpler: two components entries with alternatives "OR" on each — the "OR" indicates these are alternatives. I'll do that.

- density_range: {value: {min: 630, max: 1300}, unit_symbol: "kg/m³"}
- accuracy_class: {value: 0.3, unit_symbol: null}
- environment_classes: {value: "M2 / E2"} — this is a classification, value string "M2/E2"

- software_versions: list. Software version is a string with checksum. I could record software_versions as a list value: [{version: "1.62", checksum: "ED596201"}, ...]. The structured value shape says value can be number, {min,max}, or string. A list isn't in the shape. Maybe record as a string list? I could record as value: "1.62 (checksum ED596201); 1.64 (checksum 628A6935); 2.00 (checksum 8C64F133); 2.02 (checksum 2936EF98)". Or as multiple entries software_version_1 etc. Hmm. Maybe simpler: "software_version": {value: ["1.62", "1.64", "2.00", "2.02"]}? That deviates from the shape. I'll use a single characteristic with a string listing versions and checksums. Actually maybe better to keep it structured but as string values. Let me do:

"software_versions": {"value": "1.62 (checksum ED596201); 1.64 (checksum 628A6935); 2.00 (checksum 8C64F133); 2.02 (checksum 2936EF98)", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null, "footnote_markers": []}

That's acceptable.

MPE: Maximum Permissible Error 0.8 kg/m³ for accuracy class 0.3. That's in the accuracy class section on page 1. Record as type_level characteristic: maximum_permissible_error: {value: 0.8, unit_symbol: "kg/m³"}.

Config-level? The "condensing; open and closed locations" is a condition for ambient temperature. I could put ambient temperature as config_level with axis "installation" — conditions "open and closed locations", value {min:-10,max:55} °C, condensing. Hmm, maybe simpler to keep in type_level with a note. The condition text "condensing; open and closed locations" describes condensation conditions and locations. I'll keep it as type_level ambient_temperature_range with the value plus maybe a separate "notes" or use config_level. Let me think: config_level is for attribute × config-axis matrix. Here it's not really a matrix. I'll keep type_level and add the condition as part of the label or an extra field. The structured value shape doesn't include a condition field for type_level... The shape is {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. I could add "conditions" as extra? The rules say every characteristic value MUST be an object with that shape. Adding extra keys may be tolerated but risky. Alternatively, put ambient temperature in config_level:

config_level: [
  {attribute: "ambient_temperature_range", axis: "installation_location", values: [{condition: "condensing; open and closed locations", value: {min: -10, max: 55}, unit_symbol: "°C"}]}
]

Hmm, that could work. But it might be overengineering. The phrase "condensing; open and closed locations" is standard from the environment class spec (M2/E2 includes condensing and closed locations). I think putting it as type_level with value {min:-10, max:55} and unit °C, and maybe a separate characteristic "ambient_temperature_conditions": {value: "condensing; open and closed locations"}. That keeps the strict shape. I'll do that.

Model-level: no attributes vary per model except material. Material is in the type description. I'll put material in model_family.models[].attributes.

model_level[] — is anything varying per model? No measured characteristics vary. So model_level can be empty/omitted.
